text: Every migrated table lands in the schema of its owner in Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables: rwb_case (P3), rwb_source_data (P1), rwb_treatment (S2), rwb_asset (S5), rwb_document (P5), rwb_decision (P7), rwb_partner (S9), rwb_litigation (S4), rwb_debtsale (S6), rwb_payment (P8), rwb_writeoff (S7), rwb_comms (P6), rwb_reporting (P9), rwb_deviation (S8) and rwb_access (P4).
why: Arch v5 gives one schema per service and the Ownership Map is the run's fixed owner of every table, so the landing schema follows the owner and never the loading story.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 4, 8 and 41; ADR-014; DP-01; Ownership Map v1 sheets Services and Tables; plan/ownership.json.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.1, 9.2 and 9.3
confirm: Data architecture team confirms the table list in section 9.2 against the final LDM.
impact: 50 tables land in 15 schemas; four schemas carry no migrated row in this version.

text: The owner-side load of each migrated table is the owning service's own Flyway step in its own schema, run in the same cutover step as the P1 extract story; no new story ID is created and the step is recorded as a delta on the owning service's story set.
why: Per-service Flyway with migration ownership at the schema owner is ADR-021 and DP-15, and the plan's 14 migration stories carry no owner-side ID, so the step cannot be given an invented key.
read: Template and Rules R5.5 DP-15 and R5.7; ADR-021; plan/split_plan.json legacy RWB-DM-003 to RWB-DM-014; Ownership Map v1 sheet Services.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.1 and 9.3
confirm: TechX and the ACE team confirm with the owners when the first per-schema cutover is planned.
impact: Each owner service plans the load with its own DB and OPS work; the P1 stories keep the extract and reconciliation.

text: rwb-source-data (P1) keeps the extract, the account_key and person_key mapping and the reconciliation; the load is the owner's Flyway step in the owner's schema, run by the owner's migrator login from RWB-PLT-N011-DB, and P1 never writes another service's schema.
why: DP-01 forbids cross-schema writes and ADR-021 gives each service the migration of its own schema, while the extract and key rules already sit with P1 as the data engine.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11 and 20; ADR-021; DP-01; DP-05; DP-15; plan/split_plan.json slice RWB-PLT-N011-DB.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.1, 9.3 and 10.3
confirm: ACE team confirms the migrator role and the grant check in RWB-PLT-N011-DB.
impact: No service needs a write grant on another schema; reconciliation stays a single P1 result set.

text: Reference data (DP14) is extracted once by RWB-P1-DM014-APP and loaded by each owner: parameters and lists of values in rwb_case (P3), rule packages in rwb_decision (P7), roles and DoA limits in rwb_access (P4), templates in rwb_comms (P6), document types and retention in rwb_document (P5), EFS action codes in rwb_source_data (P1).
why: The Ownership Map assigns each reference table to one service, and the R-PREC default ruling gives only parameters and reference data to P3, so one load into one schema contradicts the map.
read: Template and Rules R3 default ruling; Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 41; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows lov_value, rule_package, delegation_limit, role, template, document_type, retention_rule, efs_ledger_outcome; Ownership Map v1 sheet Parameters.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.3 and 9.4
confirm: Data architecture team confirms the split in the P7 and P4 rule and DoA stories.
impact: Six schemas load reference rows in their own Flyway step; a reference change touches one schema.

text: The expected-return and sale-estimate records of RWB-DM-011 are held in the rwb_valuation route-decision output (S1); the case_list_row part stays in rwb_source_data (P1) and the measure_snapshot part in rwb_reporting (P9).
why: Arch v5 gives rwb-valuation the D6 route decision and the route agent output, and no other schema has a table for these records; the story names no table for them.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slide 18 (rwb_valuation: valuations, D6 route decision, route agent output); 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md RWB-DM-011 Data table; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.2 and 9.3
confirm: S1 owner confirms the route-decision columns when the RWB-DM-011 extract is designed.
impact: rwb_valuation carries one migrated record type; the story keeps its 31 December 2026 (tentative) release.

text: Each schema cuts over in the wave of its owning service, following the order in section 9.5; the 14 migration story releases keep 30 November 2026 and 31 December 2026 and are read as the latest date, not the earliest.
why: A wave 1 service cannot run on an empty schema until wave 4, and the plan's DM releases sit in wave 4 while nine services are wave 1; dates are fixed and tentative, so the order moves and no date is rewritten.
read: plan/split_plan.json slices RWB-P1-DM003-APP to RWB-P1-DM014-APP; Ownership Map v1 sheet Services (waves); Template and Rules R5.6, R5.7 and U7 (dates unchanged and tentative).
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.5 and 10.2
confirm: Programme plan owner confirms the per-wave cutover order at the wave 1 gate.
impact: Wave 1 schemas cut over in wave 1; the DM stories stay in wave 4 in the plan and act as the latest date.

text: Legacy Workbench tables stay read-only in place for the retention class of their content under the P5 retention_rule, and the data steward signs each schema's cutover before an archive date is set.
why: Version 3 requires a retention period but states none; retention_rule is the Workbench's own versioned rule table and P5 owns it, so the class comes from there rather than from a value invented here.
read: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v3.docx section 6; 04 User stories/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Stories v3.md RWB-DM-003 AC3; Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows retention_rule and document_type (P5); DP-01.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 10.2 and 10.3
confirm: Data steward and Compliance confirm the retention class per legacy table.
impact: No legacy table is dropped at cutover; the archive date is set per schema after sign-off.

text: Migrated document originals are held in Azure Blob WORM and are written only through rwb-document (P5); the metadata and every custody movement are rows in rwb_document.document and document_custody.
why: Arch v5 gives document storage to rwb-document alone, and the Ownership Map places document and document_custody with P5, so no other service stores a file or a custody row.
read: Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8 and 16 (Blob WORM, rwb-document only); Ownership Map v1 sheet Tables rows document, document_custody, document_field (P5); DP-01.
applied_in: 06 Data/Recovery Workbench Data Migration Approach v4.docx sections 9.2 and 9.3
confirm: P5 owner confirms the custody row granularity for bulk intake.
impact: The shared drives and the mailroom are read once by the intake and are not written again; RWB-DM-010 lands metadata, fields and custody in rwb_document.

text: The open promises and contact notes of RWB-DM-005 land in rwb_source_data.interaction, with the consent and contact flags in contact_point_ext; the EFS history stays a read through v_ace_efs_action.
why: The story data table names interaction and contact_point_ext, and the Ownership Map and the DP-18 default ruling put the interaction ledger with P1 rwb-source-data.
